title: ASML Up on Supply Plans; BlackRock Reports Earnings | Stock Movers
summary:
On this episode of Stock Movers:

- BlackRock (BLK) shares are responding to this morning's earnings. BlackRock reported assets under management that met the average analyst estimate and adjusted EPS and Sales beat estimates.
- ASML (ASML) shares are rising this morning after the company said it's searching for ways to produce more chip-making machines over the next two years due to soaring artificial intelligence spending. ASML said its current supply plans mean it won’t be able to fully meet demand in 2027 and 2028, and it's investigating ways to increase capacity for 2028 beyond the 30% increase previously communicated. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Resilient Growth Cushions Tech Amid Rising Rates
summary: Julia Hermann of New York Life Management tells Vonnie that the current macro and market backdrop remains favorable: economic growth is resilient, and although rates are rising, they have not yet climbed enough to threaten the growth outlook. Addressing concern that remarks from Broadcom and Intel CEOs could signal a tech selloff, she says investor focus has shifted. After years of watching for a lower limit on company investment, markets are increasingly concerned that spending—first among hyperscalers and now in chips—could become so high that it threatens free cash flow. The segment’s on-screen headlines note a worldwide memory-chip stock tumble and an ongoing chip selloff as major-bank earnings begin. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: CPI ‘Opens the Door More’ to October Fed Hike, Says PGIM’s Sockin
summary: Robert Sockin, chief US economist at PGIM, says the US economy needs two more rate hikes at a minimum and that “the broader direction is up” for interest rates even if the Federal Reserve does not move at this month’s meeting. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Fed Weighs More Hikes on Inflation Concerns
summary: Barclays senior US economist Pooja Sriram said higher interest rates are a blunt tool that tighten financial conditions and hit rate-sensitive sectors such as housing and autos first. While rising Treasury yields and the bond selloff have added restraint, she said it is unclear whether conditions are restrictive enough. With oil prices rising again, further pressure on housing and auto demand could create uneven economic damage without resolving inflation. Sriram said the Fed’s approach, reflected in September meeting minutes, is focused on managing the risk that strong demand, persistent inflation or adverse supply shocks push prices higher. The Fed appears prepared to raise rates further, though she said a hike as soon as October is unlikely. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Gold Slumps as Faster US Inflation Stokes Fed Rate Hike Wagers
summary: Gold slumped after US consumer prices jumped the most in five months, reigniting worries that the Federal Reserve will need to raise interest rates further to combat inflation.
